title: Zhou Enlai's birth chart
metaDescription: Zhou Enlai's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 14.6° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.9° separates Venus and Neptune from an exact square; at that range taste and imagination read as one mechanism. The old texts treat a square as the aspect you feel earliest and thank latest: obstruction first, competence afterwards.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 14.6° Pisces, inside the second decan (10°–20°), whose traditional sub-ruler is the Moon. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Pisces (4.6°), Venus in Pisces (18.9°), Mars in Aquarius (17.5°): thought steeped in tone and memory, attraction that works by atmosphere, effort aimed through strategy and words.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Saturn and Pluto — an opposition holding at 0.7°. Across the wheel, each body sees the other in full. The old reading is not conflict so much as permanent mutual visibility. Behind it, Venus square Neptune at 0.9°, and Mercury square Uranus at 1.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Saturn opposes Neptune while both square the Sun. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks two placements here. Mercury in Pisces at 4.6° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Pisces at 18.9° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives air 4, water 3, fire 3, and mutable 7, fixed 2, cardinal 1 across the modes. No settled placement falls in earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Jupiter was retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Leo for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.4° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 6.2°.
